title: Grab a bite
content: Meaning/Usage: To get something to eat Explanation: "A bite" refers to food. This is a pretty literal so it is simply saying to get something to eat. "When do you want to go grab a bite?" "I don't have much time, so let's grab a quick bite." "If you didn't have lunch yet, let's grab a bite to eat." A: "Did you have lunch yet?" B: "Not yet. I'm swamped with work." A: "You have to eventually eat so let's just grab a bite somewhere close." Other Common Sentences "Let's go eat." "Where should we have lunch today?" "Let's have lunch together."

examples.sentence: When do you want to go grab a bite?
I don't have much time, so let's grab a quick bite.
If you didn't have lunch yet, let's grab a bite to eat.
Not yet. I'm swamped with work.
You have to eventually eat so let's just grab a bite somewhere close.
Where should we have lunch today?
